scope: explicit cleanup and fresh synthetic attachment rebuild after activation helper crash before idle-probe receipt

failed_attachment.manual_cleanup: systemctl stop the exact disabled unit after root-owned pre-recovery state receipt was sealed

fresh_attachment_rebuild.source: fresh synthetic inert restore on the same UUID-bound disposable ext4 volume

build_and_tests.fresh_private_clone: exact commit checked out and clean before build

independent_distribution_builds.result: identical across separate output directories from the fresh source clone

interpretation: A killed activation helper can leave the separately supervised service active even though the activation receipt is incomplete; the systemd unit remains disabled and has Restart=no.

The start-intent is create-only. The affected attachment fails closed and is not retried; after an operator stops its exact unit, recovery proceeds by creating a fresh attachment from verified source state.
The strict error envelope exposes only a fixed action and allowlisted code; sudo failure, timeout, malformed output, and unrecognized failures remain generic.
limitations: The experiment covers synthetic empty idle state and process-level SIGKILL only, not abrupt host power loss, storage failure, arbitrary state, jobs, or external effects.
The first attachment is intentionally retained inert with its start-intent but no idle-probe or activation-result; it is a failed synthetic record, not a valid finalized attachment.
Provider credentials, protected datasets, Kingston, Migration v1 candidates, owner runtime, main, and research/active were not used or changed.
